mod_sources.key: B39 native national-idea names/descriptions; bounds are a locator envelope for separate sets

english_verification.review_scope: Representative opening history and flavour/name checks, bounded Wiki reading for origin and later setting outcome; no exhaustive mission audit, playtest or new Reddit/map fetch. Native English idea names/descriptions were compared by localisation key with the current Mod. Wide line ranges locate separately read passages, not exhaustive coverage. No formal validator, build, browser or gameplay test was run.

rationale.campaign_length: The current definition contains 34 direct B39 missions, excluding the B12 prologue and the Z99 successor tree.
rationale.colonization: The adventurer phase includes settlement in Escann; B39's exclusive main line focuses on conquering existing territory rather than overseas colonisation.
rationale.complexity: The campaign must balance formation, successive mercenary generations, mage resources, civil war and late army-strength conditions.
rationale.dark_story: Turning bodies into material, obedience brands and non-consensual experimentation are explicit parts of the narrative.
rationale.difficulty: The long-term systems and endgame gates are demanding; current strength has not been quantified through playtesting.
rationale.diplomacy: The adventurer company and the post-formation polity require diplomacy, but the exclusive theme leans toward warfare and internal politics.
rationale.early_pressure: B12 must meet the formation gate from its starting position as an Escanni adventurer company.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Floodborn, blood brands, mage towers and fleshcraft run through the campaign; artificers participate but do not lead it.
rationale.narrative_density: Frontier defence, the rise of magical power, Burnblood and internal crisis form a continuous sequence of reversals.
rationale.tall_play: Forges, mage towers and breeding facilities matter, but they serve the army and expansion.
rationale.trade_economy: Arms and resource supplies create economic demands, but no exclusive trade-centred loop was found.
rationale.warfare: Formation, the Alen, Escanni expansion and special mercenaries are the main loop.

identity.appearance: Not present in 1444; formed from the Brave Brothers B12 after completing the Escanni adventurer state-building decision.
identity.formation_scope: Once B12 meets the Escanni adventurer formation conditions and holds the specified area, the universal_escann_nation decision changes it to B39 and replaces the non-generic mission tree.
successors: After meeting the Escanni consolidation-war and Witch-King conditions, it may form Black Demesne Z99; Z99 has a separate exclusive mission tree.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text:
When the Wyvernhearters came to rule the lands of Cannwood and old Agradent, they also came to rule over the peoples who held ancient ties to dragon-worshipping Nimrithani... and as all Vernmen do, they took to the most exciting discoveries like a moth to a flame.

In the case of alcohol, this was literal, and Wyvernhearter mixologists came to utilize the old Nimrithani fire rituals with their own infusions. Combining the Sweetsting liqueur famous in Verne and various oils and spices with Nimrithani traditions, the cocktail, known as the Wyvern's Breath, is served as a shot on a plate saucer and set alight, causing a gust of flame to shoot out from the concoction like a breath of flame. A straw is then used to quickly consume the drink.

While complex and factually incorrect (as wyverns didn't breathe fire), the drink became popular amongst daring adventurers across Halann.

description.text:
Pushed beyond the White Walls to the poorer woodland hills of western Escann, the burgeoning Kingdom of Wyvernheart soon found wealth in their newfound role as stewards of the mighty river Alen. As with so many adventurer kingdoms, they were noble at first, guarding the river that linked Dameshead to Castonath against lurking orc and goblin marauders. But as the Age of Monsters died the Wyvernhearter kings found themselves pressed by rivals from all sides, and they turned to putting fickle and extortionate taxes on would-be merchants to ensure their survival.

Their pilferage knew no bounds, and during the 16th and 17th century as the Corinite Wars plunged Cannor proper into flame, refugees fled up the Alen to Escann where they thought wrongly that they would be safe from injustice. Instead, they found Wyvernhearter patrols with wand and musket in hand, asking for everything but the clothes off their back in exchange for 'protection'.

description.text:
"Do you hear that? Of scale and flesh bound. Fear them, son. They run on all fours yet can stand like a man. They were men, once, you know? Now warped by foul magics banned out west. They lurk the Cannwood, as if wolves, see, seeking flesh and prey like us. The wyvern-men. Don't bother running. Fight back, if you can. Bullets won't help ye, so use that bayonet of yours. Pray to Corin and avoid their great maws and their talons at all costs. If you don't, you'll be dead already, see? For their blood burns with venom off their namesake. All it takes is a drop and it'll sear you from the inside."

-Unknown Corinite refugee

description.text: When the Crimson Deluge came, all of Escann came to know that Corin was their lady and saviour, none more so than the Kingdom of Wyvernheart. Already bound to feats of glory and bravery, the people soon came to see the Floodborn: the poor mages of Escann whose lungs would fill with foul liquids every time the Deluge struck, as bearers of Corin’s suffering and determination. Those that survived went onto to become the Witch Kings of Escann, and in Wyvernheart, became the living embodiment of the divine right of kings.

description.text:
As artificery grew beyond the curated confines of the gnomish Gommo, many human artificers found themselves cast out and ridiculed for doing as humans do: pushing the limit. It is said that the first generation of immoral artificers, while few, found themselves a home in places like Corvuria and Wyvernheart. And while ordinary Corvurians were suspicious of them, as is their wont, in Wyvernheart they were treated with respect for having the bravery to push the burgeoning fields of science.

Whilst the mages created the Burnblood, it is said that the artificers of Wyvernheart perfected them... much to the chagrin of mages. By the time the magical class realized the full promise of artificery, the brave minds of Wyvernheart had already entrenched themselves with an army of mutants at their beck and call, if they so felt threatened.

description.text:
All feared him, the most powerful war wizard in Cannor: the Regent of Wyvernheart.

As all of Escann crumbled before the might of Nurcestir, Wyvernheart stood steadfast. Even while the nobles of his own kingdom plotted and schemed against the crown and each other, the Regent of Wyvernheart kept them bound to his will through callous rule and wanton violence: the only language he saw that other magical nobles understood.

But he never did it for himself. He did it for his family. For his undying love for the last of his kin: his nephew, the timid yet magically gifted king.

Still... those who threatened the crown would come to know that a new type of wyvern flew in Escann, and the Regent would bring magedeath to entire households with a thought, entire armies with a flick of a finger, slaying the most powerful Witch Kings of the age with an extension of a wrist.

description.text:
Of course, the Regent possessed no true friends; only enemies now and enemies later. When he broke through the White Walls and marched on Castonath, he was left without supplies and reinforcements and captured by King Camir of Núrcestir with the aid of his faithful companions Verindir and Erelorna. While he rotted in prison and Escann fell to Camiran rule, he heard word... his nephew had been slain in a bloody coup orchestrated by the nobles who sent him off to war in the first place.
In 1689, after a year of imprisonment, he broke out and killed his way through the Splendid Court. But when he found Camir, he did not kill him, instead offering his service. In return, the Regent was released upon his own kingdom, and alone he wiped out the entirety of the Wyvernheart nobility, whether they were suspect in the coup or not, leaving in his wake countless ruined towns, castles and palaces all across the country.

Camir, however, was not a content man, and more importantly not a man who tolerated wild dogs without a leash. The night after his last victory, all eight of the Royal Wizards of Núrcestir descended upon the Regent of Wyvernheart and slew him... but not before five of them died at the Regent’s hands. After that peace was finally restored in Wyvernheart, and the peasantry came to know stability, albeit under Camiran yoke.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who dislike mercenary management and formation gates, or who do not want body-modification and non-consensual-experimentation themes.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Establish B12 in Escann and form the country first, then balance conquest, mage politics and special-mercenary upgrades; a later move to Black Demesne is optional and is not an automatic continuation of the tree.
player_overview.overview: Start as the Brave Brothers in 1444 and become Wyvernheart after forming a kingdom in Escann. Rebuild arms production, deal with the beasts of the Cannwood, organise Floodborn mages into a ruling council and upgrade Burnblood special mercenaries through successive generations. The story shifts from frontier defence to brutal fleshcraft and a magical military state before reaching for control of Escann.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy Escanni adventurers, dark magic, special mercenaries and an exceptionally long growth arc.
signature_features: The B12 adventurer company forms B39 and receives an independent 34-mission tree.
Multi-generation Burnblood special mercenaries, breeding facilities and fleshcraft.
A Floodborn council, blood-brand abilities and mage towers jointly support a magical army.
player_overview.tagline: After founding a kingdom from an adventurer company, let mages turn wyverns, werewolves and the Crimson Deluge into a terrifying army.

reasons: The rare gameplay of upgrading mutant mercenaries through successive generations
The distinctive national identity created by the Floodborn council and blood brands
A formed country with a complete 34-mission dark-Escann story
warnings: The formation conditions must first be met as the Brave Brothers.
Mercenary and magical-resource management is involved.
Late body experimentation and the instrumentalisation of sapient life are heavy themes.

positive_indicators: Early werewolf hunts respond to a concrete threat to frontier villagers' safety.
Rebuilding arms production in Escann improves defence.
values.rationale: Rebuilding arms production and dealing with werewolves that threaten villagers serve the public good; however, later text explicitly treats orcs and other sapient beings as modification material, while Burnblood involves obedience brands, culling failed subjects and non-consensual experimentation. Conquest, monarchy and the status of mages are not themselves deductions; the severe deductions come from instrumentalising bodies and personhood.
red_flags: Mage experiments use the bodies of orcs and other sapient beings as material.
Burnblood subjects receive brands demanding complete obedience.
The modification process treats death or failure as a selection cost.
